children: Update 1:50p.m
.: Updates Liquidia shares.
Liquidia Corp.
plummeted 52% after a court ruling in its ongoing patent dispute with United Therapeutics
over its Yutrepia drug. United Therapeutics rose 13%.
The court said Liquidia's
motion to strike is denied, Judge Richard G. Andrews wrote in a court filing. The judge finds that Liquidia
has infringed claims 1 and 14 of the *327 patent, according to the  court ruling on Wednesday. The judge said the parties should submit an agreed upon form of final judgment within one week.
Liquidia
commented on the court ruling in a

on Wednesday. The company said that given the number of variables, including potential appeals and further proceedings, it's not possible at this time to reasonably estimate the range of potential outcomes or financial exposure.

"We respectfully disagree with the Court’s decision regarding claims 1 and 14 and are fully prepared to pursue all available appellate options," Roger Jeffs, CEO of Liquidia said in the statement. "As previously communicated to the Court, we intend to submit a supplement to YUTREPIA’s New Drug Application to the FDA to remove PH-ILD from the label. Our commitment to patients remains unwavering.”
United Therapeutics didn't immediately respond to a Seeking Alpha email request for comment.

"This ruling is meaningfully positive for UTHR and it is consistent with our long-held view that the company's IP estate around its treprostinil franchise is robust," RBC analyst Lisa Walter wrote in a note on Wednesday.

"At its core, we think this ruling significantly clouds the path for Yutrepia to compete freely in the inhaled treprostinil market, and if unable to sold in the U.S., or if sold with royalties to UTHR, this ruling should only benefit the Tyvaso franchise," Walter added.
Liquidia
has short interest of 13%.
MannKind (MKMD) also rose 12% on the news. United Therapeutics
markets a dry powder formulation of the lung disease therapy treprostinil, as Tyvaso DPI as part of a deal with MannKind.

title: Liquidia plunges after court ruling in United Therapeutics patent fight (update)
